answer:
Typed events work with a mapped type over `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`; no runtime change.
Probe (scratch tsc in packages/ui, removed afterwards): `Handler<E> = (e: E) => void | Effect<void, any, any> | Generator<any, void, any>` plus `onX?: Handler<...> | Effect<void, any, any>` type-checked for a plain closure using `e.currentTarget.value`, a `function*` handler yielding an Effect, and a raw `Effect.void`; a wrong member (`e.key` on a click) was rejected.
Findings: (1) E and R stay `any`, since `E` must be `never` is checked by `sleekstack check`, not tsc (README); (2) runtime lowercases `k.slice(2)`, so users write `onClick`: key names need `on${Capitalize<event>}`, not the lowercase DOM names; (3) `currentTarget` needs narrowing per tag, which the probe did with an intersection.
answer_gist: Typed events work with a mapped type over `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`; no runtime change.
